::: key-question
What health promoting or health risk behaviours are Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people living in the NEPHU catchment undertaking?
:::

::: consultation-box
- During stakeholder consultation for development of this report, cost was identified as a significant factor influencing the data – with concerns raised about vegetables being too expensive, while sugary drinks were relatively cheap. 

- The data on sugary drinks was also likely to be an under-estimation, with many people consuming them daily. In addition to being affordable, sugary drinks were seen as easily accessible enjoyment that is positive for wellbeing.   

- One local program addressing access to fruit and vegetables was the [Foodshare program](https://www.barrbuninbeek.org/programs) by Barrbunin Beek Aboriginal Gathering Place, which provides weekly boxes of fruit and vegetables for pick-up.
:::

:::{style="height: 1em;"}
:::

# Fruit Consumption

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fruit consumption meeting guidelines
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
fruit_adult <- f_read_natsihs(data_sheet = "Table 36 Adults",
                              variable   = fruit,
                              row_range  = 20:22) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(age_group = "Adults", .before = fruit,
                #
                fruit = dplyr::case_when(
                  stringr::str_detect(fruit, "Total") ~ "Total",
                  TRUE ~ fruit))

fruit_child <- f_read_natsihs(data_sheet = "Table 37 Children",
                              variable   = fruit,
                              row_range  = 7:9) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(age_group = "Children", .before = fruit,
                #
                fruit = dplyr::case_when(
                  stringr::str_detect(fruit, "Total") ~ "Total",
                  TRUE ~ fruit))

# Data wrangling
diet_fruit <- fruit_adult %>% 
  dplyr::bind_rows(fruit_child) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(fruit = factor(fruit,
                               levels = c("Met recommended fruit guideline",
                                          "Did not meet recommended fruit guideline",
                                          "Total")))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fruit consumption increase/decrease
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
diet_fruit_increase <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Fruit_Increased.csv")

# Data wrangling
diet_fruit_increase <- diet_fruit_increase %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(increased_n:stayed_about_the_same_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(similar_n = stayed_about_the_same_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(increased_n:similar_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("increased"),
                starts_with("decreased"),
                starts_with("similar"),
                starts_with("answered"))
```

- Data for this indicator were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 26% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adult survey respondents (aged 18 years and over) living in Victoria met the daily fruit consumption guidelines which recommend a minimum number of daily serves based on a person's age and sex. This equates to approximately 12,700 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adults in Victoria.

- Overall, 58% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander child survey respondents (aged 2 to 17 years) living in Victoria met the daily fruit consumption guidelines. This equates to approximately 16,000 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children in Victoria. [See Figure 9A-1](#fig_9A_1)

- Female survey respondents were more likely to have met the daily fruit consumption guidelines than males for both adults (29% vs. 23%) and children (63% vs. 56%).

- 18% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they consumed more fruit at the time of the survey than they did at the same time in the previous year, and 65% reported that their level of fruit consumption was similar to the same time in the previous year.

- Male survey respondents were more likely to have increased their fruit consumption compared to the same time in the previous year than females (22% vs. 14%). [See Table 9A-1](#tab_9A_1)

:::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" collapse="false"}
The following question was asked of all survey respondents aged 2 years and over.

- Whether fruit consumption met recommended guidelines:

    - Met recommended guidelines
    - Did not meet recommended guidelines
    - Not applicable
    - Unable to determine

:::{style="height: 1em;"}
:::
    
- Fruit consumption was assessed using the National Health and Medical Research Council’s [2013 Australian Dietary Guidelines](https://www.nhmrc.gov.au/adg). The Guidelines recommend a minimum number of daily serves based on a person’s age and sex.

- A serve of fruit is approximately 150 grams of fresh fruit or 30 grams of dried fruit.

- All drinks, beverages and juices were excluded.

:::{style="height: 1em;"}
:::

The following question was asked of all survey respondents aged 2 years and over.

Whether fruit consumption increased or decreased since the same time last year:
- Increased
- Decreased
- Stayed about the same
- Not applicable
    
Both fresh and dried fruits were included.

All drinks, beverages and juices were excluded.
::::

:::: {.panel-tabset}

### Figure 9A-1

::: {#fig_9A_1 .fig-tab-title}
**Figure 9A-1:** (A) Estimated number of people and (B) percentage of survey respondents who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander and who met recommended daily fruit consumption guidelines, Victoria, by sex and age group, 2022-2023
:::

```{r}
# Figure 9A-1
figure_number <- diet_fruit %>%
  dplyr::filter(sex != "Total" & fruit == "Met recommended fruit guideline") %>%
  #
  f_graph_survey_agesex_n(y_max    = NA,
                          y_breaks = 1000,
                          y_expand = 750)

figure_percent <- diet_fruit %>% 
  dplyr::filter(sex != "Total" & fruit == "Met recommended fruit guideline") %>%
  #
  f_graph_survey_agesex_prop(y_max    = 100,
                             y_breaks = 10,
                             y_expand = 1)

f_graph_survey_agesex_combine(figure_number  = figure_number,
                              figure_percent = figure_percent)
```

### Table 9A-1

::: {.fig-tab-title}
**Table 9A-1:** Daily fruit consumption for people who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander, Victoria, by sex and age group, 2022-2023
:::

```{r}
# Table 9A-1
diet_fruit %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(
    fruit = dplyr::case_when(
      stringr::str_detect(fruit, "Met recommended") ~ "Met guideline",
      stringr::str_detect(fruit, "Did not meet")    ~ "Did not meet guideline",
      stringr::str_detect(fruit, "Total")           ~ "Total",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_)) %>%
  #
  f_table_survey_agesex(table_header = "Fruit consumption")
```

::::

::: {.callout-note title="Data notes" collapse="false"}
- Data are obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- The 2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey collected information from Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people of all ages in non-remote and remote areas of Australia, including discrete Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander communities.

- Reported counts and percentages are a likely underestimate due to under-identification.

- Survey data do not represent exact numbers of people. As only a sample of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander people were surveyed, their results were converted into estimates for the entire Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander population, which were then rounded to the nearest 100 and/or reported as percentages.

- Unknown, not applicable, and not stated survey responses have been excluded.

- Adults are defined as persons aged 18 years and over, and children are defined as people aged 2 to 17 years.
:::

:::: {.panel-tabset}

# Vegetable Consumption

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Vegetable consumption
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
vege_adult <- f_read_natsihs(data_sheet = "Table 36 Adults",
                             variable   = vege,
                             row_range  = 24:26) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(age_group = "Adults", .before = vege,
                #
                vege = dplyr::case_when(
                  stringr::str_detect(vege, "Total") ~ "Total",
                  TRUE ~ vege))

vege_child <- f_read_natsihs(data_sheet = "Table 37 Children",
                             variable   = vege,
                             row_range  = 11:13) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(age_group = "Children", .before = vege,
                #
                vege = dplyr::case_when(
                  stringr::str_detect(vege, "Total") ~ "Total",
                  TRUE ~ vege))

# Data wrangling
diet_vege <- vege_adult %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows(vege_child) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(vege = factor(vege,
                              levels = c("Met recommended vegetable guideline",
                                        "Did not meet recommended vegetable guideline",
                                        "Total")))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Vegetable consumption increase/decrease
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
diet_vege_increase <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Vegetable_Increased.csv")

# Data wrangling
diet_vege_increase <- diet_vege_increase %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(increased_n:stayed_about_the_same_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(similar_n = stayed_about_the_same_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(increased_n:similar_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("increased"),
                starts_with("decreased"),
                starts_with("similar"),
                starts_with("answered"))
```

- Data for this indicator were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 4.5% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adult survey respondents (aged 18 years and over) living in Victoria met the daily vegetable consumption guidelines which recommend a minimum number of daily serves based on a person's age and sex. This equates to approximately 2,200 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adults in Victoria. Males were more likely to have met the guidelines than females (5.0% vs. 3.7%).

- Overall, 5.8% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander child survey respondents (aged 2 to 17 years) living in Victoria met the daily vegetable consumption guidelines. This equates to approximately 1,600 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children in Victoria. Females were more likely to have met the guidelines than males (4.5 % vs. 2.9%).

- 15% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they consumed more vegetables at the time of the survey than they did at the same time in the previous year, and 73% reported that their level of vegetable consumption was similar to the same time in the previous year.

- Male survey respondents were more likely to have increased their vegetable consumption compared to the same time in the previous year than females (18% vs. 10%).

:::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" collapse="false"}
The following question was asked of all survey respondents aged 2 years and over.

- Whether vegetable consumption met recommended guidelines:
    - Met recommended guidelines
    - Did not meet recommended guidelines
    - Not applicable
    - Unable to determine

- Vegetable consumption was assessed using the National Health and Medical Research Council’s [2013 Australian Dietary Guidelines](https://www.nhmrc.gov.au/adg).
    - The Guidelines recommend a minimum number of daily serves based on a person’s age and sex.

- A serve of vegetables is approximately half a cup of cooked vegetables (including legumes) or one cup of salad vegetables (equivalent to approximately 75 grams).

- Tomatoes were included as vegetables.

- All drinks, beverages and juices were excluded.

:::{style="height: 1em;"}
:::

The following question was asked of all survey respondents aged 2 years and over.

- Whether vegetable consumption increased or decreased since the same time last year:
    - Increased
    - Decreased
    - Stayed about the same
    - Not applicable
    
- Cooked vegetables, salad vegetables, tomatoes, and legumes were included.

- All drinks, beverages and juices were excluded.
::::

:::: {.panel-tabset}

# Sugar Sweetened Drink Consumption

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sugar sweetened drink consumption - weekly
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
sugar_adult <- f_read_natsihs(data_sheet = "Table 36 Adults",
                              variable   = sugar,
                              row_range  = 32:34) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(age_group = "Adults", .before = sugar,
                #
                sugar = dplyr::case_when(
                  stringr::str_detect(sugar, "Total") ~ "Total",
                  TRUE ~ sugar))

sugar_child <- f_read_natsihs(data_sheet = "Table 37 Children",
                              variable   = sugar,
                              row_range  = 19:21) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(age_group = "Children", .before = sugar,
                #
                sugar = dplyr::case_when(
                  stringr::str_detect(sugar, "Total") ~ "Total",
                  TRUE ~ sugar))

# Data wrangling
diet_sugar <- sugar_adult %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows(sugar_child) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(sugar = factor(sugar,
                               levels = c("Usually consumes sugar sweetened drinks",
                                          "Does not usually consume sugar sweetened drinks",
                                          "Total")))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Sugar sweetened drink consumption - daily
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
diet_sugar_daily <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Drink_Sugar.csv")

# Data wrangling
diet_sugar_daily <- diet_sugar_daily %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(consumes_sugar_sweetened_drinks_daily_n:does_not_consume_sugar_sweetened_drinks_daily_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(daily_n    = consumes_sugar_sweetened_drinks_daily_n,
                notdaily_n = does_not_consume_sugar_sweetened_drinks_daily_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(daily_n:notdaily_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("daily"),
                starts_with("notdaily"),
                starts_with("answered"))
```

- Data for this indicator were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 59% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adult survey respondents (aged 18 years and over) living in Victoria consumed sugar sweetened drinks at least once per week. This equates to approximately 29,100 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adults in Victoria. Males were more likely to consume sugar sweetened drinks at least once per week than females (70% vs. 52%).

- Overall, 54% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander child survey respondents (aged 2 to 17 years) living in Victoria consumed sugar sweetened drinks at least once per week. This equates to approximately 14,800 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children in Victoria. Females were more likely to consume sugar sweetened drinks at least once per week than males (62% vs. 47%).

- 22% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they consumed sugar sweetened drinks daily.

- Male survey respondents were more likely to consume sugar sweetened drinks daily than females (30% vs. 13%).

:::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" collapse="false"}
The following questions were asked of all survey respondents aged 2 years and over.

- Whether they usually consume sugar sweetened drinks at least once a week:
    - Usually consumes sugar sweetened drinks at least once a week
    - Never consumes sugar sweetened drinks, or usually consumes less than once a week
    - Not applicable

:::{style="height: 1em;"}
:::

- Whether they consume sugar sweetened drinks daily:
    - Consumes sugar sweetened drinks daily
    - Does not consume sugar sweetened drinks daily
    - Not applicable

- ‘Sugar sweetened drinks’ includes soft drinks, cordials, flavoured mineral waters, caffeinated energy drinks, sports drinks, and electrolyte drinks.

- Alcoholic drinks, fruit juices, vegetable juices, flavoured milks, tea, and coffee are excluded.
::::

:::: {.panel-tabset}

### Figure 9A-5

::: {#fig_9A_5 .fig-tab-title}
**Figure 9A-5:** (A) Estimated number of people and (B) percentage of survey respondents who identified as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander and who consume sugar sweetened drinks at least once per week, Victoria, by sex and age group, 2022-2023
:::

```{r}
# Figure 9A-5
figure_number <- diet_sugar %>%
```

# Artificially Sweetened Drink Consumption

```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Diet drink consumption - weekly
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
diet_adult <- f_read_natsihs(data_sheet = "Table 36 Adults",
                             variable   = diet,
                             row_range  = 36:38) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(age_group = "Adults", .before = diet,
                #
                diet = dplyr::case_when(
                  stringr::str_detect(diet, "Total") ~ "Total",
                  TRUE ~ diet))

diet_child <- f_read_natsihs(data_sheet = "Table 37 Children",
                             variable   = diet,
                             row_range  = 23:25) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(age_group = "Children", .before = diet,
                #
                diet = dplyr::case_when(
                  stringr::str_detect(diet, "Total") ~ "Total",
                  TRUE ~ diet))

# Data wrangling
diet_diet <- diet_adult %>%
  dplyr::bind_rows(diet_child) %>%
  #
  dplyr::mutate(diet = factor(diet,
                              levels = c("Usually consumes diet drinks",
                                         "Does not usually consume diet drinks",
                                         "Total")))

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Diet drink consumption - daily
# Data from ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Read in NATSIHS data
diet_diet_daily <- f_read_natsihs_sex("Indicator_Vic_Sex_Drink_Diet.csv")

# Data wrangling
diet_diet_daily <- diet_diet_daily %>% 
  dplyr::rowwise() %>% 
  dplyr::mutate(answered_n = sum(across(consumes_diet_drinks_daily_n:does_not_consume_diet_drinks_daily_n))) %>% 
  dplyr::ungroup() %>% 
  #
  janitor::adorn_totals(fill = "Total") %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename(daily_n    = consumes_diet_drinks_daily_n,
                notdaily_n = does_not_consume_diet_drinks_daily_n) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::mutate(across(daily_n:notdaily_n,
                       ~ . / answered_n * 100,
                       .names = "{.col}_prop"),
                #
                answered_prop = answered_n / answered_n * 100) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::rename_with(~ stringr::str_replace(., "_n_prop$", "_prop"), ends_with("_n_prop")) %>% 
  #
  dplyr::select(sex,
                starts_with("daily"),
                starts_with("notdaily"),
                starts_with("answered"))
```

- Data for this indicator were obtained from the [2022-23 ABS National Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Health Survey](https://www.abs.gov.au/statistics/people/aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-peoples/national-aboriginal-and-torres-strait-islander-health-survey/latest-release).

- Overall, 34% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adult survey respondents (aged 18 years and over) living in Victoria consumed artificially sweetened (diet) drinks at least once per week. This equates to approximately 16,800 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander adults in Victoria. Females were more likely to consume artificially sweetened drinks at least once per week than males (38% vs. 29%).

- Overall, 19% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander child survey respondents (aged 2 to 17 years) living in Victoria consumed artificially sweetened drinks at least once per week. This equates to approximately 5,200 Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander children in Victoria. Males were more likely to consume artificially sweetened drinks at least once per week than females (18% vs. 15%).

- 8.1% of Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander survey respondents living in Greater Melbourne reported that they consumed artificially sweetened drinks daily.

- Female survey respondents were more likely to consume artificially sweetened drinks daily than males (11% vs. 4.9%).

:::: {.callout-tip title="Question/s asked for this topic" collapse="false"}
The following questions were asked of all survey respondents aged 2 years and over.

- Whether they usually consume artificially sweetened (diet) drinks at least once a week:
    - Usually consumes artificially sweetened (diet) drinks at least once a week
    - Never consumes artificially sweetened (diet) drinks, or usually consumes less than once a week
    - Not applicable

:::{style="height: 1em;"}
:::

- Whether they consume artificially sweetened (diet) drinks daily:
    - Consumes artificially sweetened (diet) drinks daily
    - Does not consume artificially sweetened (diet) drinks daily
    - Not applicable

- ‘Artificially sweetened drinks’ includes soft drinks, cordials, flavoured mineral waters, caffeinated energy drinks, sports drinks, and electrolyte drinks that have been sweetened with artificial sweeteners (e.g. saccharin, aspartame, sucralose).

- Fruit juices, vegetable juices, flavoured milks, tea, and coffee are excluded.
::::
